title: [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois..., pages 650 bis à 787, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: section 16°, 'Réflexions sur le théorème de Fermat'. U_n is the affine Fermat curve over Q: x_0^n+x_1^n+x_∞^n=0 in P^2 with all coordinates invertible. Via the Kummer isogeny x↦x^n of the torus T = G_m^{0,1,∞}/G_m, it is the inverse image of U_1 = {x_0+x_1+x_∞=0} ≅ P^1−{0,1,∞}. Its compactification Û_n is the projective Fermat curve. Û_n → Û_1 ≅ P^1 is a (Z/n)^2-cover of degree n^2, ramified with index n over 0,1,∞ and étale elsewhere.

This page computes the genus. Since U_n → U_1 is finite étale of degree n^2, Euler characteristics multiply: χ(U_n) = n^2 χ(U_1). Here χ(U_1) = 2−3 = −1 and χ(U_n) = (2−2g_n) − 3n, because there are 3n cusps (n over each of 0,1,∞). Hence 2(g_n−1) = n^2−3n, so g_n = 1 + n(n−3)/2 = (n−1)(n−2)/2. This gives g_1 = g_2 = 0, g_3 = 1 and g_n > 1 for n ≥ 4.

Conclusions drawn:
- Every U_n is hyperbolic, hence 'anabelian'. The complete curves Û_n are anabelian for n ≥ 4; Û_3 is an elliptic curve.
- If the anabelian yoga holds (the section conjecture), rational points of U_n correspond to splittings of the fundamental exact sequence 1 → π_1(U_n ⊗ Q̄) → π_1(U_n) → Γ_Q → 1 (371) other than the 'sections at infinity', i.e. the cuspidal sections attached to the 3n cusps.
- Grothendieck characterises the non-cuspidal sections intrinsically: s is non-cuspidal iff the centraliser in π_1(U_n) of s(Γ_Q^+) is trivial, where Γ_Q^+ = Ker(χ: Γ_Q → Ẑ^*) = Gal(Q̄/Q(μ_∞)). The reason: a cuspidal section lands in a decomposition group containing the inertia Ẑ(1), and Γ_Q^+ acts trivially on that inertia.
- So Fermat (for U_n) should be reflected in, and would follow unconditionally from, the non-existence of non-cuspidal sections of (371). On the next page he proposes attacking this by successively finer 'approximations' of π_1(U_n) ⊂ π_1(P^1−{0,1,∞}) ('M_{0,3}') and of N_{1,1}, i.e. via Galois–Teichmüller / Lie-algebra filtrations.
errors: The marginal note 'π_1(Û_1) ≃ M_{0,3}' is a slip if the hat is really there. Û_1 = P^1 is simply connected; it is π_1(U_1) = π_1(P^1−{0,1,∞}) that Grothendieck denotes by the (profinite) group of type (0,3).

Minor: 'pour n≥3' is used for the sign-symmetric Fermat equation x_0^n+x_1^n+x_∞^n=0. For even n, U_n has no real points and its cusps are not real either, so the statement is trivial there. The section-theoretic version for even n also follows from the real section conjecture (now a theorem). The substantive case is odd n, where the equation is equivalent to classical FLT.

Characterising non-cuspidal sections by triviality of the centraliser of s(Γ_Q^+) is stated without proof. It is plausible and in line with later results (Nakamura, Mochizuki) on centralisers and decomposition groups at cusps.

missed.claim: An explicit, pre-Wiles programme to prove FLT by showing the Fermat-curve extension (371) has only cuspidal sections, regarded as a statement provable without the full section conjecture, attacked through refinements of π_1(P^1−{0,1,∞}). The same strategy was later pursued independently (Ihara on the Fermat tower; Ellenberg-type nilpotent obstructions; Wickelgren et al. on Fermat curves). This page documents Grothendieck's priority for the idea, but it is not a new mathematical result.

missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Historical credit: Grothendieck explicitly linked the section conjecture, the Fermat tower and Diophantine Fermat. This is the motivation of current work on nilpotent section obstructions for Fermat curves.

missed.claim: The centraliser criterion for non-cuspidal sections, stated using Γ_Q^+ = Ker(cyclotomic character), appears here before its later appearances in the literature.

deep.surprise_reason: The mathematics is routine (genus formula) plus the well-known section conjecture. What is mildly notable is the explicit unpublished proposal to attack Fermat via section non-existence for the Fermat tower, including a centraliser criterion for cuspidal sections. Similar ideas were developed later independently, so this is mainly a priority/historical detail.
transcription_corrections: Marginal note under (371) reads 'π_1(Û_1) ≃ M_{0,3} !'. Mathematically this should be π_1(U_1); the hat may be a slip by Grothendieck.
The annotation '3n' above 'pts' (3n points at infinity) is an insertion: 'localisés en les 3n pts à l'infini de U_n'.
The underbraces read 'EP de Û_n' and 'EP de U_n' under the left side, and 'EP de Û_1' and 'EP de U_1' under the right side (EP = caractéristique d'Euler–Poincaré).
